title: Domain pack: software and product development
description: Rules scaled to the size and risk of the task -- a one-file script does not need an enterprise release process. See PRD Phase 15.

rules.title: State the problem before proposing the implementation
rules.purpose: Prevent building the first plausible solution to an unstated problem.
rules.requirement: brief.normalized_problem_statement describes what is broken or missing, distinct from brief.goal describing what will be built.
rules.evidence_requirement: The two fields are not restatements of each other.

rules.title: Acceptance criteria exist and are scaled to risk, not maximal by default
rules.purpose: Avoid forcing heavyweight process onto small, low-risk tasks while still requiring a real Definition of Done.
rules.requirement: acceptance.criteria contains at least one 'must' criterion with a concrete verification_method; for routing.risk_level 'low', criteria may be minimal, but they may not be empty.
rules.evidence_requirement: acceptance.criteria is non-empty and each criterion is independently checkable.
rules.source_or_rationale: PRD Phase 15: 'Acceptance criteria... Do not force an elaborate enterprise process onto a small script.'

rules.title: Record non-obvious architecture decisions
rules.purpose: Preserve the reasoning behind a choice that a future maintainer could not otherwise recover.
rules.scope: Software tasks with routing.risk_level of 'medium' or higher.
rules.requirement: Any decision that would surprise a future maintainer (dependency choice, data-model shape, backward-compatibility trade-off) is recorded with its rationale.
rules.evidence_requirement: A decision record or equivalent note exists for each such choice.

rules.title: Backward compatibility is considered for changes to existing interfaces
rules.purpose: Prevent silently breaking existing callers or users.
rules.scope: Software tasks that modify an existing public interface, schema, or CLI.
rules.requirement: A change to an existing interface states whether it is backward-compatible and, if not, calls this out as a breaking change rather than leaving it implicit.
rules.evidence_requirement: The deliverable or changelog states compatibility impact explicitly.

rules.title: Code handling external input avoids common injection classes
rules.purpose: Prevent OWASP-Top-10-class vulnerabilities from being introduced.
rules.scope: Software tasks that produce code handling external input.
rules.requirement: Code that handles external input is checked for injection, XSS, path traversal, and similar OWASP Top 10 classes before being reported complete.
rules.evidence_requirement: A note or tool output showing this check was performed.
rules.source_or_rationale: General safety rules; PRD Phase 13 threat model.

rules.title: Tests are scaled to risk and actually executed, not just written
rules.purpose: Prevent claiming correctness based on code that looks right but was never run.
rules.requirement: Any 'tests pass' claim in status.verified_facts must be backed by an actual test-run command and its output, not by static review alone.
rules.evidence_requirement: The command and a summary of its output (pass/fail counts) are recorded.
rules.source_or_rationale: PRD Phase 19: 'Test meaningful invariants... every skipped test must have a narrow, documented environmental reason.'

rules.title: Release/packaging steps are scaled to actual distribution risk
rules.purpose: Avoid demanding CI/CD and package publishing for a throwaway script, while still requiring it for a published package.
rules.scope: Software tasks whose expected_deliverables include a published package, release, or public repository.
rules.requirement: Packaging, versioning, and release notes are addressed proportionally to whether the deliverable is actually meant to be published or shared.
rules.evidence_requirement: The deliverable's distribution plan matches its actual audience.
rules.source_or_rationale: PRD Phase 15: 'Release engineering... Scale requirements to risk and task size.'

rules.title: Completion is evidence-based, not assumed from code existing
rules.purpose: Prevent conflating 'I wrote the code' with 'the feature works'.
rules.requirement: status.completion_status of 'complete' requires each 'must' acceptance criterion to have a corresponding entry in status.verified_facts.
rules.evidence_requirement: A 1:1 mapping exists between must-criteria and verified_facts entries.
